todaysEvents.summary: Saudi reroutes crude via Sohar transfers
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 16 that Aramco is offering more Arab Light/Medium/Heavy crude via ship-to-ship transfer off Oman's Sohar port after a Sep 11 drone strike shut the East-West pipeline to Yanbu; Ras Tanura loadings have doubled.

todaysEvents.summary: Hormuz crossings stay in single digits
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 17 that Strait of Hormuz tanker crossings remain in single digits per LSEG data, as owners avoid the route and shuttle vessels move crude out of the Gulf to reload onto larger tankers outside the strait.

todaysEvents.summary: Record VLCC ordering wave reshapes routes
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 17 that shipowners ordered 217 VLCCs in 2026 versus 93 in 2025, a $20bn+ spree, as Hormuz risk pushes longer Atlantic-to-Asia routes, record freight rates, and an ageing fleet toward renewal.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: After the shelved talks resume, the Oman framework is signed and monitored; a restored, verified reopening lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained into early November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Talks remain shelved or resume without regional consensus; traffic stays selective under Iranian fees and sanctions pressure; Brent holds $85-105 and JKM stays elevated while QatarEnergy seeks replacement LNG.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Iran enforces its threatened Hormuz exclusion zone, talks fail, or the tanker war widens into a broader multi-front exchange; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
